title: Aurum Alpha profile of an RFC 9068 JWT access token
description: The token the identity provider issues and the relying party forwards to a backend, per standards/060-auth.md AU2. RFC 9068 fixes the shape; this file pins what the RFC leaves optional. The backend VERIFIES the signature against the provider's JWKS rather than decoding the token — a parsed but unverified token is no check at all. The validation order is RFC 9068 section 4's: typ, iss, aud, signature, exp. Registered JWT and OIDC claims keep their RFC spelling and NumericDate encoding. additionalProperties is deliberately absent: RFC 9068 section 2.2.2 permits private claims and a real provider emits some, so the closed set is the required list plus the prohibitions stated in these descriptions. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

iss.description: THE IDENTITY PROVIDER. Half the link key of AU3, and where the JWKS is fetched from. Matched byte for byte against the configured issuer string, never resolved by discovery in a split-horizon deployment.

sub.description: The provider's subject, and the other half of the link key. Opaque, never displayed, never parsed. Unique and never reassigned only WITHIN its issuer, which is why the pair is the key and this value alone is not (AU3).

aud.description: The resource indicator of the ONE backend this token is for, obtained with RFC 8707 'resource' or a provider audience mapper. MUST be enforced (RFC 9700 section 2.3): without the check, a token issued for one backend replays against another. A single string, or the array form RFC 7519 permits.

client_id.description: RFC 9068 section 2.2. The relying party that obtained this token — the proxy's client, not the backend's.

exp.description: NumericDate. Five minutes, because this is an internal hop rather than a user session. This is also AU5's revocation backstop.

jti.description: Unique per token, so a replay is detectable.

auth_time.description: NumericDate of the actual human authentication. Optional in RFC 9068 section 2.2.1 and REQUIRED by this profile: an application requires step-up for a sensitive operation without understanding how authentication happened, and 082 DR2's fifteen-minute window reads this claim.

amr.description: OIDC authentication methods reference — what the person actually did. Optional in RFC 9068 section 2.2.1 and REQUIRED by this profile. Read for step-up decisions, never for authorization.

sid.description: The provider's login session. Not defined by RFC 9068 and REQUIRED by this profile, as the registered OIDC claim for the job: correlation, back-channel logout (AU5), and the tenant binding key of AU8.

email.description: Cached display attribute, permitted by RFC 9068 section 2.2.2 under its registered claim name. NEVER a foreign key (AU3).

email_verified.description: AU4's provider-is-source mode requires this true before it writes a user. An unverified address is a claim about a mailbox that belongs to somebody else.

name.description: Cached display attribute. Never a key.

scope.description: PROHIBITED AS AN AUTHORIZATION INPUT. RFC 9068 section 2.2.3 permits it and a provider emits what it is configured to emit, so the schema cannot forbid the field. Nothing in an application reads it to decide access.

groups.description: PROHIBITED AS AN AUTHORIZATION INPUT, for the reason on 'scope'. A groups claim read for access would make every application's access control depend on provider configuration, which is the failure this standard exists to prevent.

roles.description: PROHIBITED AS AN AUTHORIZATION INPUT, for the reason on 'scope'. Roles are the application's, per 070 RB1.

entitlements.description: PROHIBITED AS AN AUTHORIZATION INPUT, for the reason on 'scope'. Entitlements are derived under the billing standard, per 075 BL4.
